application: Each edit applies independently through repo/tools/firmware_patch.py patch(raw, module=0, region='code', address=..., expect=..., replace=...) from pristine stock. Combined application replicates the patcher's finalization (header-mirror sync + trailer CRC); the framework build (work/patches/framework) applies both via the sibling .patch files dac_fix_1_branch.patch / dac_fix_2_cave.patch and stamps its own stock+1 date.
bug: Byte at 0x0300411E counts failed dac_write I2C transfers since the last DAC start. At >=2, dac_write (0x03060c4c) and dac_read (0x03060d28) silently skip all DAC access. The counter is never decremented or reset on success (only zeroed by the DAC-start routine 0x03051a4e, once per playback session), so two transient I2C errors at any point in a session permanently disable DAC control until a full stop / reboot.

edits.after: beq 0x03060d8e   ; success: detour to the reset trampoline
edits.before: beq 0x03060d1c   ; success: skip the failure increment, join tail

edits.after:
strb r0, [r5, #1]   ; r0 == 0 on the success path, r5 == 0x0300411d -> counter = 0
b 0x03060d1c        ; rejoin stock tail (movs r0, #0; bus release; return)
edits.before: bx lr ; bx lr   ; alignment padding after dac_read, zero references in all 82 modules (the referenced stubs at 0x03060d98/0x03060d9a are untouched)

fix: Reset the counter on a successful dac_write so it counts CONSECUTIVE failures: retarget dac_write's success branch to a 4-byte trampoline in a provably unreferenced alignment stub, which stores the already-zero result register to the counter and rejoins the stock tail. Two consecutive failures still disable DAC control (dead-DAC protection preserved).
name: dac-error-counter-reset-on-success

verification.byte_diff_vs_stock: exactly 9 bytes: 0x3a3c0 (1), 0x3a43a..0x3a43d (4), 0xd00000..0xd00003 (trailer CRC, 4); header-mirror region untouched
verification.disassembly: Capstone on the patched module 0; encodings independently reproduced by rz-asm at the target addresses
